blocks.caption: Methods of preparing halogenoalkanes
rows: Halogenation of an alkane in light
Addition of a hydrogen halide to an alkene
pyridine; the by-products are gases that escape, leaving pure product
3CH3CH2OH + PBr3 -> 3CH3CH2Br + H3PO3; CH3CH2OH + PCl5 -> CH3CH2Cl + POCl3 + HCl
CH3CH2OH + KBr + H2SO4 -> CH3CH2Br + H2O + KHSO4
the acid and KBr make HBr in the flask

blocks.text: The KBr method is commonly used for bromoalkanes and iodoalkanes: the acid first reacts with the potassium halide to give the hydrogen halide, which then reacts with the alcohol. Phosphoric acid is preferred for iodoalkanes because, unlike concentrated sulphuric acid, it does not oxidise iodide ions to iodine.

blocks.alt: Six boxes around CH3CH2-X, each with an arrow to it: ethane + Cl2 in light; ethene + HBr; ethanol + HCl with ZnCl2; ethanol + SOCl2 with pyridine; ethanol + PBr3 or PCl5 (with their equations); ethanol + KBr + H2SO4, with H3PO4 for iodoalkanes.
blocks.caption: Six ways to make a halogenoethane (original summary of the book's methods).
blocks.long_description: One route starts from an alkane, one from an alkene and four from an alcohol. The alcohol routes all replace the -OH group by a halogen, using a hydrogen halide, thionyl chloride, a phosphorus halide, or a hydrogen halide made in the flask.

blocks.title: Interesting information
blocks.text: Some marine algae and phytoplankton, such as Trichodesmium, turn bromide from seawater into volatile organobromine compounds. These reach the atmosphere, take part in the global bromine cycle and contribute to the depletion of stratospheric ozone. (The book names bromoethane; the compound most often described is bromomethane.)

blocks.prompt: Give two methods of converting methanol into chloromethane.
blocks.explanation: Any two: CH3OH + HCl (ZnCl2 catalyst) -> CH3Cl + H2O; CH3OH + SOCl2 (pyridine) -> CH3Cl + SO2 + HCl; CH3OH + PCl5 -> CH3Cl + POCl3 + HCl.

blocks.prompt: Give the reactions of propan-1-ol with SOCl2 and with PBr3.
blocks.explanation: CH3CH2CH2OH + SOCl2 -> CH3CH2CH2Cl + SO2 + HCl; 3CH3CH2CH2OH + PBr3 -> 3CH3CH2CH2Br + H3PO3.

blocks.prompt: Can fluoromethane be made from methane and fluorine gas?
blocks.explanation: Not in practice: fluorine reacts explosively with methane, giving a mixture of fluorinated products, carbon and HF rather than controlled monosubstitution.

items: From alkanes (X2, light), alkenes (HX) or alcohols (HCl/ZnCl2, SOCl2, PX3, PCl5, KBr + acid).
SOCl2 gives gaseous by-products; H3PO4 is used for iodoalkanes.
